text:
sam: Quick sync — want a short, actionable cutover + acceptance checklist for Dedicated pools we can hand to Sales and Oncall. Goal: reduce back-and-forth during pilot.

anya: +1. I can draft the checklist. Need clear lead times and what passes the smoke runner.

mike: Keep acceptance tests tiny and automatable. Suggested minimal suite:
- 5m steady load @ expected QPS: 95th < target
- p99 within allowed degradation
- KV/prefix cache smoke (basic read/write)
- Simulate preemption and verify graceful fallback
Gate = runner exit code.

sam: Good. Also want a Billing mapping: reserved slots vs burst add-ons vs overage. Elaine?

elaine: I'll own billing language. Proposal: base invoice = reserved capacity; burst SLA = opt-in add-on (X sustained extra throughput for Y minutes); overage = per-minute billing beyond reserved unless SLA purchased.

jordan: Ops handover stuff: PagerDuty owner for 24h post-cutover (explicit person), monitoring dashboard link, rollback steps, and prewarm activation instructions. I can template the PD note.

ops-bot: I volunteer to cover the 24h monitoring window for first two pilots. Will add a PD template and checklist.

sam: Forecast windows? How much lead time for new pools and for resizing existing reservations?

anya: Recommend: new pool = 14 days minimum; resize = 72 hours. Make them hard gates.

mike: Can we embed a single smoke-runner script and require it to upload a JSON report to the runbook? That makes CI gating easy. Example snippet:
```
# quick k6 smoke example
k6 run --vus 20 --duration 5m smoke-test.js || exit 1
```
Runner exit code -> pass/fail and artifact URL required in runbook.

deploy-bot: created draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/cutover-acceptance-draft (v0.1)

elaine: For Sales messaging: we need deterministic phrasing. "Reserved capacity" vs "Burst SLA" vs "Best-effort burst" — customers must opt into Burst SLA at sale time. I'll prepare one-paragraph sellable language.

sam: Two leadership policy choices to surface with the roadmap entry:
1) Offer paid burst guarantees (opt-in) or only soft best-effort for everyone?
2) Autoscale cooldowns: platform default or allow per-customer tuning?

jordan: Ops prefers a centralized default for cooldowns to reduce surprises. Allow overrides but require Ops review and a support fee.

elaine: I prefer paid burst opt-in. Keeps pricing simple and avoid accidental promises.

anya: Action list I'm adding to the draft doc:
- Forecast windows (14d / 72h)
- Smoke-runner + artifact requirement + example snippet
- PD handoff template + 24h owner field (ops-bot will add)
- Billing mapping draft (assigned to elaine)
- Policy options text (burst SLA opt-in + cooldown override workflow)

mike: Small note: run acceptance in staging against an isolated pool that mirrors production config. Add a tiny k6/hey script to repo for Sales/Solutions to run during demo.

ops-bot: I'll add the PD template and schedule a rota for 24h coverage for pilots.

sam: Timeline: pilot with 1-2 customers in ~3 weeks. After pilot, bake runner into CI and refine playbook. We'll flag the 2 policy decisions for leadership review next week.

elaine: I'll sync with Finance tomorrow on invoice wording and draft numbers for burst add-on.

mike: Once anya pushes the checklist, I can convert the smoke-runner to a single binary that outputs pass/fail + report URL.

anya: Will push draft by EOD and link the runner example. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
